## CRITICAL guardrails
- The board + its cards live in the Nxeon platform DB on THIS box (/opt/nxeon). Code/data changes for Soul Pilates happen on **51.79.226.200**.
- Get root SSH creds for .200 from the platform DB: server row id `cmsc9l72y000ghl7iyd87u5ja`; password = `decryptSecret(server.rootPasswordEnc)` using lib/crypto-box.ts (run a node script in /opt/nxeon; connect with the `ssh2` Client as root). **ASSERT the IP is 51.79.226.200 before running ANY command on it.**
- Any `docker compose up` for Soul Pilates MUST include `--env-file prod.env` (compose project `soulpilates`, file `docker-compose.prod.yml`). Missing it makes ${VARS} (JWT key, Mongo string) resolve empty → backend crash-loops (IDX10703). This exact mistake took the business down before.
- Work on the **staging** stack `/opt/soulpilates-staging` first for code changes. Do NOT deploy to Soul Pilates PRODUCTION — instead, prepare the prod deploy and HAND THE EXACT COMMAND BACK in your report for the user to run.
- Verify Soul Pilates prod stays healthy (https://soulpilates.com.vn returns 200) before AND after anything you touch.
- Mongo: container `soulpilates-prod-mongo`, db `soulpilates`. Back up any document before you modify it.

## Workflow rule (board is a living record)
For EACH card: FIRST move Ideas → In progress + comment you're starting; when done, move to Review + comment with findings/what changed/what needs the user. Mechanics (node script in /opt/nxeon, `import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client"`):
- move: `db.card.update({ where:{id}, data:{ columnId, position:0 } })`
- comment: `db.cardComment.create({ data:{ cardId:id, authorName:"Claude", body } })`

## The 2 cards
1. **Customer unsubscribed by accident** (id `cmsft7sqc0002hln8s5m3lzga`) — Two parts:
   (a) IMMEDIATE, SAFE data fix: customer id `6a54b26a1d3c92cadac61bf5` unsubscribed from emails by accident and wants back in. Find their client document in the SP Mongo, back it up (print it), and set their email-subscription flag back to subscribed / clear the unsubscribe flag. This is a targeted single-document, reversible update — do it carefully on the live Mongo after asserting the IP.
   (b) FEATURE: add an "Email subscribed" toggle to every customer profile (the /admin/client-profile page), ON by default, that unchecks when a customer unsubscribes. Investigate the SP CRM's client-profile page + the existing unsubscribe mechanism + the Mongo client schema. Implement on STAGING; hand the prod deploy command back.
2. **New metric** (id `cmsftkuaw0006hln8a3r7oohu`) — new per-instructor analytics: (i) total packages sold attributable to each instructor (customers who bought a package after attending that instructor's class), and (ii) average classes taught per package bought per instructor (a ratio) — to reveal which instructor best converts attendees into package buyers. Investigate the SP Mongo (attendances/bookings, packages, instructors collections) and the existing admin analytics screens, then add this metric. Implement on STAGING; hand the prod deploy command back.

## If blocked
If you cannot get SSH creds / reach .200 / the classifier blocks a live-business action, STOP that step, move the card to In progress (not further), and post a comment + report exactly what you found and the precise commands the user needs to run. Never guess or fake a live-business change.

Report back: per-card findings, what you changed on staging, the customer-resubscribe outcome, the exact Soul Pilates PROD deploy command(s) for the user, and each card's final column.

model Server {
  id                  String        @id @default(cuid())
  name                String
  label               String? // customer-facing nickname (rename)
  hostname            String
  vmid                Int?          @unique
  status              ServerStatus  @default(PENDING)
  ipAddress           String?       @unique
  sshPort             Int?          @unique
  rootPassword        String?
  rootPasswordEnc     String?
  isFree              Boolean       @default(false)
  autoRenew           Boolean       @default(true)
  gameVariant         String? // game-server type/loader (e.g. paper, carbon, bepinex) — see lib/game-config
  gameConfig          Json? // per-game settings values (validated against the family schema)
  suspendedNote       String?
  // WHY a server is suspended: "UNPAID" | "ABUSE" | "ADMIN". Null = never suspended.
  //
  // `suspendedNote` used to be the only signal, and nothing consumed it, so every
  // suspension looked identical to the billing engine. Two live consequences:
  // (1) `terminateOverdue` selected on `status: "SUSPENDED"` alone, while the
  //     renewal sweep EXCLUDES suspended servers — so an admin suspending a
  //     paid-up customer pending an investigation meant they were never charged,
  //     never warned, their term lapsed, and 13 days later their VM and all its
  //     data were destroyed with a "prolonged non-payment" notice they had never
model Card {
  id          String           @id @default(cuid())
  boardId     String
  board       Board            @relation(fields: [boardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  columnId    String
  column      BoardColumn      @relation(fields: [columnId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  title       String
  description String           @default("") // markdown
  type        CardType         @default(FEATURE)
  priority    CardPriority     @default(NORMAL)
  labels      String[]         @default([])
  assignee    String? // free-text ("me", "claude", a name)
  position    Int              @default(0)
  archivedAt  DateTime?
  createdAt   DateTime         @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime         @updatedAt
  attachments CardAttachment[]
  comments    CardComment[]

  @@index([boardId])
  @@index([columnId])
}

model CardAttachment {
  id         String         @id @default(cuid())
  cardId     String
  card       Card           @relation(fields: [cardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  filename   String // original name shown to the user
  storedName String // on-disk name (uuid + ext) under the board upload dir
  mime       String         @default("application/octet-stream")
  sizeBytes  Int            @default(0)
  kind       AttachmentKind @default(FILE)
  createdAt  DateTime       @default(now())

  @@index([cardId])
}

model CardComment {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  cardId     String
  card       Card     @relation(fields: [cardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorName String   @default("")
  body       String
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([cardId])
}

DATABASE_URL=<set>
AUTH_SECRET=<set>

# Staging & release workflow — setup guide

This repo now supports a proper **staging → GitHub → production** flow so you
never develop directly on the live system again.

```
edit on a branch (staging dir)  →  deploy-staging + test
   →  push to GitHub  →  merge to main  →  deploy-prod
```

## What's already been set up
- **Full backup** taken before any changes → `/opt/backups/soulpilates-<timestamp>/`
  (`db-mongodump.archive.gz` + `full-soulpilates.tar.gz`, verified).
- **Git repo** initialized at `/opt/soulpilates` with a baseline commit; branches
  `main` (production) and `develop` (work). Secrets/data are gitignored.
- **Staging stack files**: `docker-compose.staging.yml`, `staging.env.sample`.
- **Scripts**: `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`, `scripts/deploy-prod.sh`,
  `scripts/sync-staging-db.sh`.

## One-time setup you need to do (needs your accounts / DNS)

### 1. Push the repo to GitHub
```bash
cd /opt/soulpilates
# create a PRIVATE repo on github.com first, then:
git remote add origin git@github.com:<you>/soulpilates-crm.git
git push -u origin main
git push origin develop
```

### 2. Create the staging working directory (separate from live)
Staging is a **second checkout** so editing/testing never touches the live source:
```bash
git clone /opt/soulpilates /opt/soulpilates-staging      # or clone from GitHub
cd /opt/soulpilates-staging
git checkout develop
cp staging.env.sample staging.env       # then fill in — see step 3
```

### 3. Fill in `staging.env` (own secrets, NOT prod's)
Generate fresh values so staging is fully isolated:
```bash
# JWT + passwords
openssl rand -hex 32          # → JWT_SECRET
openssl rand -hex 16          # → MONGO_PASSWORD / REDIS_PASSWORD / RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY
# VAPID keypair for web push (or reuse a throwaway pair)
```
Set `SMTP_TEST_REDIRECT_TO=` to your own inbox (test emails go there, never to
customers). Keep `STRIPE_ENABLED=false` unless testing payments with `sk_test_…`.

### 4. Point a staging subdomain at it (nginx + cert)
Add DNS `staging.soulpilates.com.vn` → this server, then an nginx server block
(mirror the prod one) with a TLS cert, proxying:
- `/api` and `/soulpilates-public` → the backend/rustfs (`127.0.0.1:8491`, `:6424`)
- everything else → the frontend (`127.0.0.1:3819`)

Recommended: protect the whole staging host with HTTP basic-auth so it isn't public.

### 5. Bring staging up + load data
```bash
cd /opt/soulpilates-staging
scripts/deploy-staging.sh develop     # builds :staging images, starts the stack
/opt/soulpilates/scripts/sync-staging-db.sh   # copies prod data in (PII scrubbed)
```

## Day-to-day workflow
1. In `/opt/soulpilates-staging`, branch off develop: `git checkout -b feature/x`.
2. Make changes there and `scripts/deploy-staging.sh feature/x` to test.
3. Commit + push: `git push origin feature/x`; open a PR into `main` on GitHub.
4. After review/merge, publish live: on **`/opt/soulpilates`** run
   `scripts/deploy-prod.sh` (pulls `main`, rebuilds, recreates the app containers).

> The live production dir (`/opt/soulpilates`) should only ever be updated via
> `deploy-prod.sh` (i.e. from merged `main`), not hand-edited.


#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Build + run the STAGING stack from the staging working dir
# (/opt/soulpilates-staging). Safe: never touches the production containers.

BRANCH="${1:-develop}"

[ -f staging.env ] || { echo "!! staging.env missing — cp staging.env.sample staging.env and edit."; exit 1; }
STG_API_URL=$(grep -oP '(?<=^PUBLIC_API_URL=).*' staging.env)

echo "→ starting staging stack…"
docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml --env-file staging.env up -d

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Publish to PRODUCTION (soulpilates.com.vn). Run from /opt/soulpilates.

echo "→ smoke test…"
